texts.preamble: C.A. Das vs The Controller on 11 September, 2013 Author: P.R.Ramachandra Menon Bench: P.R.Ramachandra Menon In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr.Justice P.R.Ramachandra Menon Thursday, The 26Th Day Of September 2013/4Th Aswina, 1935 WP(C).No. 22894 of 2013 (J) ---------------------------- Petitioner: ------------------------- C.A. Das, Aged 63 Years, S/O.K.M. Chellappan, Residing At .T.C.30/981, Pettah, Thiruvananthapuram. By Adv. Sri.Rajesh P.Nair
texts.facts: The petitioner is aggrieved of the course and proceedings pursued by the respondents 2 and 3, whereby two weighing machines belonging to the petitioner were simply seized by them on 07.09.2013 leaving the petitioner in dark. The case of the petitioner is that the seizure was effected without offering any explanation or reasons, but for as a measure of highhanded act on the part of the respondents, which is turn is under challenge in this writ petition.
texts.arguments: 2. Today when the matter came up for consideration, the learned counsel for the petitioner points out that after filing writ petition, the petitioner has been served with show-cause notice bearing No. 266 of 2013 dated 11.09.2013, though it was served to the petitioner only on 19.09.2013, raising various allegations and infringement of the statutory provision. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there is absolutely no merit or bonafide in the show-cause notice and that petitioner has already filed a detailed explanation/reply before the respondents.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 2. Today when the matter came up for consideration, the learned counsel for the petitioner points out that after filing writ petition, the petitioner has been served with show-cause notice bearing No. 266 of 2013 dated 11.09.2013, though it was served to the petitioner only on 19.09.2013, raising various allegations and infringement of the statutory provision. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there is absolutely no merit or bonafide in the show-cause notice and that petitioner has already filed a detailed explanation/reply before the respondents.
